top_stories.title: Intel Plunges on Weak Q3 Guidance, Drags Down Semiconductor Sector
points: Intel (INTC) dropped 26-26.6% in a single week after missing Q3 guidance due to data center manufacturing bottlenecks, its worst day since the 1970s.
The decline dragged down the broader semiconductor sector, with some chip names losing up to 30%.
Yahoo Finance adds that Intel sank 20% specifically after a weak Q4 outlook overshadowed an otherwise solid Q3 earnings beat.

unique_angles.point: Intel's Q3 results actually beat expectations, but weak forward Q4 guidance drove the selloff.

top_stories.title: Tech Earnings Rout Drives Broad Market Selloff
points: Alphabet (Google parent, GOOG/GOOGL) fell 12.2% for the week after Q3 results missed consensus, signaling weakness in its core business.
Nasdaq Composite fell about 2% for the week and another 2.9% in a single Friday session as AI-related trades reversed and big tech earnings disappointed.
S&P 500 lost roughly 0.57% for the week but fell 2.1% in the Friday rout; Dow dropped 0.85% for the week and 1.3% on Friday.
Other major decliners included ServiceNow (down 34%), Fortinet (down 24%), Reddit (down 30-36%), F5 (down 26%), Roblox (down 20%), plus double-digit drops in Salesforce, Twilio, and Guidewire.
Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and SpaceX all contributed to the rout via disappointing outlooks and rising AI-related cash burn concerns.

unique_angles.point: Russell 2000 (small-cap stock index) gained 1.3% for the week, suggesting investors rotated out of tech and into smaller-cap, non-tech stocks.
Alphabet suffered its worst month ever, losing $766 billion in market value in October alone, hitting valuation levels not seen in over a decade.

items.title: Federal Reserve Holds Rates Steady Amid Dissent
points: The Fed kept interest rates at 3.75%-4.00% on Wednesday, citing strong economic activity.
Two officials dissented: Fed Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack.

Core PCE Price Index (inflation gauge excluding volatile food and energy costs) rose 0.3% month-over-month in September, matching August's pace and estimates; the headline PCE index (including food and energy) rose 0.5%.
Initial jobless claims unexpectedly fell last week, signaling continued labor market strength.
U.S. GDP grew faster than initially estimated in Q3, reinforcing the Fed's cautious stance on further rate cuts.

items.title: Anthropic Files for IPO Amid AI Stock Jitters
points: AI company Anthropic filed for an IPO (initial public offering, when a private company first sells shares to the public) on Nasdaq, reporting $16.3 billion in annual revenue.
The filing comes during a volatile period for AI-related stocks as market sentiment toward the sector sours.

items.title: Sector Rotation and Global Market Moves
points: Healthcare (+3.1%), Utilities (+2%), and Materials (+2%) led S&P 500 sector gains, while Telecom fell 8.5% and Information Technology dropped 1.8%.
Germany (+2.5%) and France (+2.4%) gained, Japan rose 1%, but China fell 2.5% amid ongoing economic concerns.
Crude oil (WTI) fell 0.3% to $102.95/barrel; gold dropped 3.1% to $3,884.90/ounce; natural gas surged 9.2% to $2.883.
Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other major cryptocurrencies fell 3-5% amid broader risk-off sentiment.

items.title: Binance Suffers Record $6.3 Billion Crypto Heist
points: Binance was hit by a $6.3 billion theft, the largest cryptocurrency heist in history, allegedly linked to North Korea.
About $3 billion has been frozen, but a significant portion of losses may be permanent; Binance says it will cover losses and is working with law enforcement.
The key unanswered question is whether AI played a role in executing the attack, which could have major implications for corporate security and insurance industries.
Bitcoin prices fell following the theft, raising concerns that AI-powered heists could become a routine corporate threat.

items.title: Google's AI Search Summaries Crush Website Referral Traffic
points: Google's shift from linking out to websites toward AI-generated summaries and chatbot answers is sharply reducing referral traffic across the internet.
Reddit CEO Steve Huffman said search referral traffic was down 'meaningfully' last quarter due to Google's AI-driven search mode.
The trend, dubbed 'Google Zero' (fear of search referral traffic approaching zero), is a widespread concern for content sites and businesses reliant on search traffic.
In response, Reddit plans to require user logins/accounts, shifting its strategy away from dependence on Google-driven traffic.

sections.title: Tech Earnings Rout Triggers Market Selloff
points: 1. Intel (INTC) dropped 26.6% in a single week after reporting weaker-than-expected Q3 guidance tied to data center manufacturing bottlenecks. The stock suffered its worst day since the 1970s.
2. Alphabet (GOOG/GOOGL) fell 12.2% after posting Q3 results below consensus expectations, indicating weakness in its core business.

3. ServiceNow (NOW) and Fortinet (FTNT) each plummeted over 34% and 24% respectively; other notable losers included Reddit (down 36%), F5 (down 26%), and Salesforce, Twilio, and Guidewire all posting double-digit declines.
4. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite declined 2% for the week, underperforming the broader S&P 500's 0.57% decline and the Dow's 0.85% drop, suggesting a flight from high-growth stocks.

sections.title: Economic Data Remains Mixed Despite Rate Hold
points: 1. The Federal Reserve kept interest rates in the 3.75%-4.00% range on Wednesday, as expected. Fed communications noted economic activity expanding at a strong pace, but two officials dissented.

2. Core PCE Price Index (a measure of inflation excluding volatile food and energy prices) rose 0.3% month-over-month in September, unchanged from August and in line with estimates; the broader PCE Price Index including food and energy climbed 0.5%.
3. Initial jobless claims unexpectedly fell during the past week, signaling continued labor market strength.
4. U.S. GDP grew faster than initially estimated in Q3, supporting the Fed's decision to maintain its cautious approach to further rate cuts.

sections.title: Sector and Global Market Dynamics
points: 1. Healthcare (+3.1%), Utilities (+2%), and Materials (+2%) led S&P 500 sectors higher, while Telecom fell 8.5% and Information Technology dropped 1.8%, reflecting sector rotation away from growth.

2. International markets showed mixed performance: Germany and France gained 2.5% and 2.4% respectively, Japan rose 1%, but China fell 2.5%, signaling ongoing concerns about the world's second-largest economy.
3. Crude oil (WTI) declined 0.3% to $102.95/barrel; gold fell 3.1% to $3,884.90/ounce; natural gas surged 9.2% to $2.883, indicating energy market volatility.
4. Bitcoin, Ethereum, and other major cryptocurrencies fell 3-5% during the week amid broader risk-off sentiment in growth-oriented assets.

issues.subject: Morning Brief: The Binance heist's biggest unanswered question

headlines: Binance suffered a $6.3 billion heist—the largest cryptocurrency theft ever—allegedly linked to North Korea, with $3 billion frozen but substantial losses potentially permanent.
Google's shift to AI-generated search summaries instead of links is decimating referral traffic to websites; Reddit's search traffic dropped significantly, causing its stock to fall 30%.
S&P 500 fell 2.1%, Nasdaq dropped 2.9% on Friday as earnings disappointments and AI trade reversals crushed tech stocks.
The critical unanswered question: How much did AI play a role in the Binance heist, and what does this mean for corporate security and insurance?
Reddit plans to require user accounts and logins to combat traffic losses, accepting it cannot rely on Google referrals returning.

sections.title: The Binance Heist: Crypto's Biggest Unknown
points: $6.3 billion stolen in coordinated attack linked to North Korea—largest known heist in cryptocurrency history and potentially human history by value.
Attack was complex and well-coordinated; company says it will cover losses and work with law enforcement, though a 'solid chunk' may be permanently gone.
Critical unknown: role of AI in the attack. If AI played significant role, insurance industry backstopping corporate risk and banking sector could face new vulnerabilities.
Bitcoin prices fell following the theft; raises questions about whether AI-powered heists will become routine corporate threats going forward.

sections.title: Google's AI Search Shift Destroying Website Traffic
points: Google shifted from linking to websites toward AI-generated summaries and chatbot dialogue to answer search queries directly, reducing need to visit external sites.
Reddit CEO Steve Huffman stated search referral traffic 'was down meaningfully' in latest quarter as Google's AI mode halted the traffic flow that previously sustained the platform.
The problem affects entire internet ecosystem, not just Reddit—'Google Zero' (traffic approaching zero) is now a widespread fear across content sites and businesses reliant on search referrals.
Reddit stock plummeted 30% Friday following earnings; company responding by planning to require user logins, shifting strategy away from dependence on Google traffic.

sections.title: Market Selloff on Earnings Disappointment
points: S&P 500 fell 2.1%, Dow dropped 1.3%, Nasdaq sank 2.9% as week's earnings crushed stocks and AI trade that once supported market gains reversed.
Alphabet (Google parent) suffered worst month ever with $766 billion in October losses; stock hit a level for trading metrics not seen in over a decade.
Reddit stock fell 30%, Roblox tanked 20% after Q3 earnings; Intel sank 20% as weak Q4 outlook overshadowed Q3 beat.
Magnitude of declines reflected broader tech sector pressure as Amazon, Alphabet, Meta, and SpaceX all contributed to rout through disappointing outlooks and cash burn concerns.
